title: Prediction of unmeasured bias curves with predictive intervals: single card vs near-optimal ensemble vs Laplace vs learned cross-device discrepancy
written: 2026-10-19, before any E4 fit, smoke run or evaluation was executed
hypothesis: When a device's card is fitted to a subset of its I-V curves, (H1) an ensemble of near-optimal cards or a Gauss-Newton Laplace approximation gives predictive intervals for the unmeasured curves whose 90% coverage is between 0.70 and 0.95, and (H2) at least one such method, or a discrepancy model learned on other DEV devices, predicts the unmeasured curves with lower paper RRMS than the single best-fit card.

data.devices: REAL_DEV only (12 devices, out/research/explore/real_split.json). REAL_TEST is not loaded by any E4 code (e4_fit.py refuses non-DEV tags).
data.curves: frozen published-baseline inclusion set (card_eval.include_tags); measured Id cleaned and trimmed by metrics.curve_trim

splits.vd (primary): train = every included Id-Vg curve + the included Id-Vd curve at the highest gate bias; held out = the other included Id-Vd curves (3 per nMOS; per pMOS: 4 for pmos_L0p35_W0p55, 3 for pmos_L0p35_W5, 2 for the other DEV pMOS)
splits.vg (secondary): train = every included Id-Vd curve + Id-Vg at Vd = 0.01 and 1.85; held out = Id-Vg at Vd = 0.37, 0.74, 1.11, 1.48

parameter_boxes.p43 (primary): out/cold_loop/full/round_1/spec.json (43 parameters, box centered on the multiplier-one card; no card fitted to measured curves enters the box or the starts)

fit_procedure: src/cryoml/explore/e4_heldout.fit_device: CMA-ES (6000 evals, sigma0 0.3, from box center) + 2 further CMA-ES seeds (3000 evals each) on the mean train-curve RRMS; each result polished by bounded TRF with batched NGSpice forward-difference Jacobians (local step 0.01, max_nfev 40); 8 perturbation starts (best polished card + N(0, 0.3^2) on active local coordinates, TRF max_nfev 20). Every polished card is a member and is re-simulated exactly. SINGLE = member with the lowest train objective. Laplace at SINGLE: covariance (J_e^T J_e / sigma^2 + I / 0.5^2)^-1 in active local coordinates, J_e = Jacobian of per-point train errors (sim - meas)/den, sigma = RMS of those errors at SINGLE; 64 draws clipped to the box and simulated. Seed 20261019.

methods.single: point = SINGLE card curves; no interval
methods.ens: members with train objective <= 1.10 x SINGLE's; point = pointwise median; interval = equal-weight Gaussian mixture of members, member sd = member train sigma x mean |member prediction| over the curve
methods.ens_env: same members; interval = pointwise min-max (reported, not a candidate)
methods.laplace: point = mean of the Laplace draw curves; interval = mixture of draws with sd = SINGLE train sigma x mean |SINGLE prediction| over the curve
methods.laplace_param: draw quantiles without the noise term (reported, not a candidate)
methods.conformal: point = single; interval = single +/- q x sigma x scale, q = equal-device-weight quantile (with (n+1)/n correction) of |meas - single| / (sigma x scale) on the other DEV devices' held-out points (leave-one-device-out)
methods.crossinterp (non-learned control): single + (meas - single) measured on train curves at the bias points where they cross the held-out curve, linearly interpolated along the sweep voltage with a zero anchor at 0 V; conformal interval as above (crossinterp_conformal)
methods.learned: single + scale x kernel-ridge prediction of (meas - single)/scale, trained on the other DEV devices' held-out points (leave-one-device-out; every 3rd point; features: family, log10 L, log10 W, curve bias, sweep voltage, crossinterp residual / scale, distance to nearest cross point, log10 train sigma; RBF length and ridge chosen by inner leave-one-device-out from {0.5,1,2} x {0.01,0.1,1}); interval = point +/- q x sigma x scale with q from inner leave-one-device-out residuals

metrics.heldout_rrms: per device: mean over held-out curves of the paper per-curve RRMS (RMSE / mean |meas| on trimmed points); all-device mean over the 12 DEV devices (nMOS, pMOS, combined also reported); a non-finite held-out prediction makes the device NaN
metrics.coverage_0.9: per device: fraction of trimmed held-out measured points inside the central 90% interval; all-device mean (also 0.5, 0.8, 0.95)
metrics.width_0.9: per device: mean (hi - lo) / den over the same points; all-device mean
metrics.identifiability: singular values of the weighted train Jacobian at SINGLE (effective rank at 1e-2 and 1e-3 of the largest), fraction of the held-out sensitivity in the sloppy subspace (s/s_max < 1e-2), near-optimal member count and per-parameter local spread (count > 0.1), Laplace posterior sd count > 0.1 (all reported, no criterion)

control_baseline: single (one best-fit card, the standard practice); crossinterp is the non-learned data control for the learned method

criterion.C1_calibration: all-device mean coverage_0.9 in [0.70, 0.95] AND all-device mean width_0.9 <= 4.0 x single's all-device held-out RRMS
criterion.C2_accuracy: method's all-device held-out RRMS <= 0.95 x single's AND lower than single on >= 8 of 12 devices
criterion.C3_learned_vs_data_control: for 'learned' only: all-device held-out RRMS <= crossinterp's
criterion.CONTINUE: some candidate method satisfies C1, C2 and C3
criterion.PARTIAL_CALIBRATION_ONLY: no method satisfies all, but some candidate satisfies C1 (continue only as a calibration component of another direction, not as a standalone contribution)

secondary_reported_without_decision: correlation of held-out error with heldout_sens_in_sloppy_frac across devices
smoke: a light run (4 DEV devices, reduced budgets) checks the code only; its numbers do not enter the decision
